Every check of the opening and of the compiled verifier that is not a check of an earlier phase.
The setup and commitment checks are B1 to B10 and B17 of \cref{tab:gen-bus-checks}; they are
listed here only where this part adds something. ``Attack'' is a prover, committed word or proof
that a verifier \textbf{without} the check accepts although it should not; where the check does
not protect soundness this is said rather than invented. The dossier cites the specification row
by row for the setup only; for the other rows the specification's column gives what its closing
list (\code{08:100}) says of them, as the text after the table reads it, and a dash where that
list says nothing. The messages named are those of \cref{tab:gen-opening-whir}.

The blueprint's \lean{Sizes.Admissible} must contain the rate window and the stacking window
(S-rate and S-window; \cref{f:bus-admissible}).

\paragraph{The specification's closing list.} \code{08:100}: ``Accepts if every check above passed:
the caps, the one bus root for both sides, the nonzero count root, every sumcheck's rounds and final
value, the public-input line, flock's reduction, and the PCS opening.'' Against
\cref{tab:gen-opening-checks}: ``the caps'' omits the rate window and the stacking window (S-rate,
S-window); ``every sumcheck's rounds'' is not a check in either verifier (W1); ``the PCS opening''
stands for M1 to M7, W2 to W5 and, absent from Annex B altogether, G1. Absent from the specification
and present in both verifiers: the canonical encodings (B2, B3, B10 of \cref{tab:gen-bus-checks};
R2), full consumption (R4), grinding (G1, G2). The blueprint's \lean{verify} inherits the omissions of
the specification it is ``written from'' (\code{bp:1216}) unless Layer 12 lists the checks of
\cref{tab:gen-opening-checks}; its six mutations (\code{bp:1238-1239}) exercise M6 and the scalars
only (\cref{f:opening-mutation-tests}).

\paragraph{Negative results.} Checked, no finding: the query sampling is exactly uniform ($d$-bit
chunks of a uniform 192-bit string, $d ≤ 28$, $⌊192/d⌋ ≥ 6$ chunks per squeeze, a valid weaker
bound: the citation check finds $d ≤ 26$ at the supported sizes, so $⌊192/d⌋ ≥ 7$;
\code{whir.rs:1175-1193}, \code{py:943-951}); the two verifiers derive $n_{\mathrm{lanes}}$, the
block lengths and the leaf widths from the announced sizes (\code{whir.rs:2061-2066, 2084, 2213};
\code{py:1040, 1048-1049}); both floor $μ$ at 15 (\code{witness.rs:97}, \code{py:890}); the Python's
\code{derive_config} and the Rust's \code{configs_for_rate} give the same ladder for every $(μ, ρ)$
in the window (\cref{sec:gen-opening-probe-params}).
